title: Finite constructible stratifications have a limiting common fibre-product refinement
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $r\in\mathbb N$, $U,O_0,\ldots,O_{r-1}$ open subschemes of $X$ with $U\subseteq O_j$, and $S_j$ finite stratifications [def-constructible-stratification] of $O_j$ whose locally closed strata are constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]. There is a finite constructible stratification $T$ of $U$, and for every stratum $T_k$ a choice of one stratum $S_{j,a(k,j)}$ of each $S_j$, and a limiting fibre-product cone [def-pc-fibre-product] over the maps $U\to X$ and $S_{j,a(k,j)}\to O_j\to X$, whose vertex is $T_k$ and whose projection to $U$ is its immersion. If $r\ne0$, every retained vertex is nonempty. If $r=0$, retain the single identity stratum, even when $U$ is empty.

source.place: Finite-reductions Step 6, common strata; Stacks Tags 054I, 02V0, 005H

proof.text: Induct on r, starting with the identity one-stratum partition of U. At the successor step restrict the new partition to U by Stratification.pullback and intersect it with the previous partition using Stratification.inter. These existing constructions retain the actual pullback schemes and their immersion maps, not only their point sets.

source.place: Tag 054I; finite-reductions Step 6, iterated pullback refinement

proof.text: Prove the limiting-cone assertion at the same time. Build the old cone from every test cone by omitting the new factor, lift to its vertex by the induction hypothesis, lift the new-factor map to the restricted stratum, and take their pullback lift. Projection equations follow from pullback.lift_fst and pullback.lift_snd. Uniqueness follows from pullback.hom_ext; the immersions to U are monomorphisms. For r=0 use the projection to U as the unique lift.

source.place: Fibre-product universal property, finite iteration in common-strata argument Step 6

proof.text: When r is nonzero restrict the finite index set to vertices with a point, and enumerate this subtype by Fin n. A point of U is still covered because any stratum containing it has a point. Pairwise disjointness, constructibility and the same limiting cones restrict to this subtype. For r=0 retain the original identity stratum.

theorem finite_stratification_wide_pullback {X : Scheme.{u}} (r : ℕ) (U : X.Opens)
    (O : Fin r → X.Opens) (S : ∀ j, Stratification (O j).toScheme)
    (hU : ∀ j, U ≤ O j) :
    ∃ (T : Stratification U.toScheme)
      (a : Fin T.n → ∀ j, Fin (S j).n)
      (c : ∀ k, WidePullbackCone (stratificationWideArrows U O S (a k)))
      (hp : ∀ k, (c k).pt = T.domain k),
      (∀ k, eqToHom (hp k).symm ≫ (c k).π none = T.immersion k) ∧
      (∀ k, Nonempty (IsLimit (c k))) ∧
      (r ≠ 0 → ∀ k, Nonempty (T.domain k)) ∧
      (r = 0 → T.n = 1 ∧ ∀ k, IsIso (T.immersion k))
